title: Scaling rhythm & commitment alignment for Dedicated Autoscale — Q2 planning
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Goal: produce a compact, executable Q2 roadmap that aligns capacity commitment windows with autoscale policies, cost guardrails, and OKRs for Dedicated customers. This ticket synthesizes cross-functional inputs (ENG reliability spikes, Console UX constraints, sales commitment windows) into a two-sprint deliverable set and a reproducible cadence for future quarters.

Scope items (what this ticket will deliver):
- Recommended cadence and guardrails for reservation windows and burst reservoirs (policy matrix by customer tier).
- Canonical autoscale policy templates (predictive warm pools, reactive burst, and hedged fallback) with cost/latency tradeoffs documented.
- Ops runbook for canarying policy changes, rollback thresholds, and telemetry contracts.
- OKR alignment doc: measurable outcomes and success metrics for rollout.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive predictive warm pooling reduces latency but increases committed cost; we will recommend tiered prewarm ratios and a 2-week experiment window per cohort.
- Reactive burst reduces committed spend but increases tail latency under sudden spikes; fallback routing to cheaper model variants is proposed as a mitigation.
- Control plane complexity vs. platform simplicity: prefer policy templates over bespoke configs for first rollout to accelerate adoption.

Cross-functional owners: PM (Evelyn Park) coordinates; Eng leads for runtime & autoscale (Sanjay Patel), Infra for capacity purchasing (Maya Chen), Console/Product Design (Priya Nair) for admin UX, Sales/RevOps (Jordan Lee) for customer commitment inputs.

comments: 2026-02-19 — Kickoff: Alignment meeting w/ Eng (Sanjay), Infra (Maya), Design (Priya) and Sales (Jordan). Agreed to run two parallel experiments: (1) predictive warm pool ratio tuning, (2) fast-fail fallback routes for surge events. Action: ENG to run warm-pool spike throughputs and produce cost delta matrix by 2026-03-05. — Evelyn

2026-02-26 — ENG update (Sanjay): Spike results uploaded (see Spike results link). Predictive warm ratio 0.15 reduces p95 latency by ~28% for tier-1 workloads but increases committed spend by ~12%. We recommend pilot on 3 customers. Created ENG-7634 for runtime scheduler changes needed. — Sanjay

2026-03-02 — Design review (Priya): Console mockups for new 'capacity rhythm' settings reviewed. Feedback: surface cost impact estimate inline, add 'suggested policy' prescriptive option. Created design ticket DES-210 for small UI polish. — Priya

2026-03-06 — PM review: Draft OKRs posted to PRD. Primary objective: Reduce p95 generation latency for committed Dedicated workloads by 20% without increasing platform-wide committed spend by >5%. Secondary objective: 90% canary success rate and <1% rollback rate for policy changes. Assigned metrics owner: Maya. — Evelyn

2026-03-10 — Risk note (Jordan): Sales requests shorter reservation windows (monthly) for pilot customers. This conflicts with predictive warm pools which favor longer horizons. Decision: allow a 'pilot' mode with shorter windows but a higher prewarm multiplier; monitor unit economics closely. Added dependency on PM-909761 (billing cadence experiment). — Jordan

2026-03-12 — Roadmap draft finalized and shared with Execs; requested a slice for 2 enterprise customers to onboard adaptive warm pools in April pilot. Next: finalize runbook and sign-off from Security for telemetry retention. — Evelyn
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated roadmap doc with timeline and owners published in Confluence
Three autoscale policy templates documented, each with cost/latency tradeoff table
Runbook for canaries and rollback thresholds validated in staging and linked to incident playbook
Telemetry contract defined (metrics, SLO thresholds, dashboard links) and ownership assigned
Commitment from Sales for two pilot customers and an identified internal champion per pilot
success_metrics: p95 inference latency for pilot workloads reduced by >=20% vs baseline
Committed spend delta across Dedicated fleet <= +5% after pilot adjustments
Canary success rate >= 90% and rollback < 1% during policy rollouts
Pilot adoption: 2 paying customers on adaptive warm pools by 2026-05-01
risks: Underestimated reservation economics causing material margin erosion if warm pools scale up too broadly
Control plane changes for policy templating could introduce config drift without strict validation
Short reservation windows requested by customers reduce predictive model effectiveness
Telemetry gaps could delay detection of regressions during canary runs
